note: OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts policies deployed by us (OZ example code, third-party, not audited by us): testnet runs builds of tag v0.8.0, mainnet runs builds of tag v0.7.2. A rule scoped to one of these would hand its signers the account-auth half of that contract's admin calls (set_threshold, install, uninstall), so the builder refuses it. packages/policy-synth/src/config.ts lists the same addresses (SPENDING_LIMIT, OZ_THRESHOLD, SUPERSEDED_OZ_POLICIES); config.test.ts holds the two together.

testnet.command: stellar contract build --package <package> (stellar-cli 27.1.0, rustc 1.98.1 stable, the tag's rust-toolchain.toml; soroban-sdk 28.0.0)

testnet.deployer: a throwaway key funded by friendbot
testnet.extendNote: 26 October 2026: each instance and its code extended to ledger 8,386,5xx (about mid April 2027).

changesFromV072: In packages/accounts/src/policies, v0.7.2..v0.8.0 changes code in spending_limit only: a transfer of amount 0 is always permitted (before, it was refused once the cached total exceeded a lowered limit), and MAX_HISTORY_ENTRIES drops from 1000 to 815 (the most a single ledger entry holds). simple_threshold and weighted_threshold change in comments only. The Policy trait (policies/mod.rs) is identical; smart_account adds the ContextRuleType variant CreateContractExternalRef, so a v0.8.0 policy also reads the rules of a v0.7.2-line account. Every wasm hash differs because the workspace moved from soroban-sdk 26.1.0 to 28.0.0.

superseded.why: testnet moved to the v0.8.0 builds above. Kept recognised on read (a rule already capped or thresholded by them is still reviewed) and in POLICY_CONTRACTS (no rule may be scoped to them); no new rule attaches them.
